newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures consolidated, tracking Bunds, to settle near their lows as the market waited for the outcome of Tuesday's long-awaited US FOMC gathering.
One analyst said some investors had lightened their positions ahead of the meeting but that the market had been overbought.
"It was a logical correction after last week's strong advance but so far it's not jeopardising the bullish trend," he said.
Analysts were divided over the chance of an immediate rate hike by the Fed.

A poll by Reuters of 30 economists showed 17 expected a rate rise on Tuesday while seven saw one when the FOMC meets again on November 13. Five analysts expected the status quo for the coming months while one saw an increase at the start of 1997.
One analyst warned the market could react badly, with the long end worst hit, if the FOMC failed to raise the Fed funds rate by an expected 25 basis points on Tuesday.

"If it just maintains the status quo, the market could take it badly," he said. "People want the Fed to be the gatekeeper against inflation." But he said a lot would depend on how the Fed worded its comments.

PIBOR also weakened but did not lose as much ground as the 10-year notionnel. One analyst said the three-month interest rate contract was less vulnerable to the outcome of the Fed meeting even if the authorities raised rates. "It would not put into jeopardy the monetary easing cycle in Europe," he said.
One analyst saw the 10-year bond future range-bound on Tuesday between 123.70 and 124.00 ahead of the FOMC meeting.

The franc gave up most of the day's gains against the mark as the German currency came off lows hit in early trading, following a weekend meeting of European finance ministers that saw more progress toward European monetary union.
The franc was trading at 3.3865 per mark late in the day after hitting an intraday high of 3.3810, its best level since July 11, and little changed from 3.3862 per mark late on Friday.
